title: Mathematical programs with complementarity constraints
contribution: Short survey arguing that standard NLP solvers (SQP first, IPMs with small modifications) solve MPCCs reliably, organized around the equivalence of strong stationarity and the KKT conditions of the NLP reformulation.
problem_entry: Attacks the received verdict that solving MPCCs as NLPs is numerically unsafe because MFCQ fails at every feasible point (pp. 15-16).
key_idea: Strong stationarity equals KKT of the NLP; the unbounded multiplier set is a ray with a minimal element, so SQP and penalized/relaxed IPMs can be analysed with standard tools (pp. 16-18).
assumptions: MPCC with 0 <= x1 perp x2 >= 0; SQP local result needs consistent QPs (mixed-P lower level); PIPA perturbation only without bi-active constraints (p. 17).
proof_devices: multiplier substitution nu_hat = nu - X xi with explicit minimal xi (eqs. 3-5), p. 16
two-case split of the SQP local proof: iterate on vs off the complementarity manifold, p. 17
relaxation tau <-> penalty rho equivalence, p. 17
experiments: none new; reports 150+ problems solved with quadratic convergence for all but two, IPMs about 80% with defaults (pp. 16-17)
positioning: Credits Scholtes, Anitescu, Raghunathan-Biegler, Liu-Sun, Benson-Shanno-Vanderbei; special-purpose MPCC methods require significantly more work (pp. 15-17).
writing: Slogan section titles (The NLP Revolution; SQP Lead the Way), lively low-hedging prose, core claim restated as the underlying theme in the conclusion (pp. 16-18).
limits_future: Open: global convergence, convergence to B-stationary points, avoidance of C-stationary limits, global solutions for brittle fracture (p. 18).

title: Solving mathematical programs with complementarity constraints as nonlinear programs
contribution: Introduces the MacMPEC library (137 problems) and the filtermpec AMPL interface and shows that SQP solvers solve MPECs as NLPs robustly, outperforming IPMs and comparing favourably with special MPEC solvers (read as Dundee TR NA/210, 2002).
problem_entry: Tests empirically the argument that MFCQ failure rules out NLP solvers for MPECs, after disappointing past numerics (TR pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Off-the-shelf NLP solvers on the NLP form with z1'z2 <= 0 (not = 0), relaxed complementarity linearization plus restoration, via an AMPL interface adding slacks only when needed (TR pp. 1, 3, 5-6).
assumptions: MPEC with slack-reformulated complementarity (no loss of CQs or second-order conditions); quadratic SQP convergence to the basic multiplier needs consistent QPs (TR pp. 1, 3).
proof_devices: minimal (basic) multiplier and ray structure of the multiplier set, TR pp. 2-3
explicit SQP iterates z(k)=z(0)/2^k on a 2-variable example: linear rate for z1z2=0 vs one step for <= 0, TR p. 3
closed-form lower-level solution map of dempe to classify limits (not even B-stationary), TR pp. 11-12
experiments: 137 MacMPEC problems, 4 NEOS solvers; catastrophic vs soft failure taxonomy; remove-and-rerun attribution test with z1'z2 <= 1e-2; Dolan-More profiles on iterations and CPU with failures as asymptote; multiplier-size profile; tentative comparison with published MPEC solvers, generator online (TR pp. 7-17).
positioning: Corrects Conn-Gould-Toint and Ferris-Pang on LUBRIF (failure not due to complementarity); neutral review of smoothing, penalty, PIPA, implicit and Fisher-Burmeister approaches (TR pp. 3-4, 10).
writing: Claims stamped at present and tentative by design; closing positions SQP solvers as the benchmark for future MPEC solvers (TR pp. 1, 17-18).
limits_future: IPMs fail on about 15%; perturbation (3.4) under investigation; linear convergence to B-stationary points on ralph1 and scholtes5; IPM modifications planned (TR pp. 6, 13-14, 17-18).

title: The penalty interior-point method fails to converge
contribution: A three-variable MPCC on which PIPA converges to a feasible nonstationary point although the theorem's hypotheses [SC] and [NS] hold, traced to a trust-region bound tied to infeasibility, with a standard ared/pred remedy (read as arXiv math/0310357v1).
problem_entry: Targets the published convergence theorem of PIPA, a method used in finance, target classification and electricity markets (pp. 1-2, 4).
key_idea: The direction-finding bound ||dx||^2 <= c(||F|| + y'w) shrinks with feasibility and freezes progress in the controls; let the algorithm control the radius by ared/pred instead (pp. 2, 8-9).
assumptions: Theorem hypotheses [SC], [NS], bounded Hessians, sigma > 0, bounded alpha; simplified PIPA with fixed sigma; Qk = 0 for simplicity, argued robust to small PSD Qk (pp. 3-5).
proof_devices: minimal example (3.1) whose solution satisfies [SC] and [NS], p. 4
Lemma 3.1: five invariants (3.2)-(3.6) by induction from a fixed start and parameters, pp. 4-7
explicit LP basis inverse and multipliers to certify the active set, p. 5
series lower bound tau >= 5/9 on the line-search root, pp. 6-7
geometric-sum bounds on the limit (x >= -0.4828, y <= 1.4828) and check that the limit satisfies the hypotheses, pp. 7-8
experiments: Example and PIPA coded in AMPL (looping extension); 10 iterates with ared and pred tabulated, confirming the bounds (pp. 7-8).
positioning: States directly that the example contradicts [16, Theorem 6.1.17] (pp. 4, 8); frames the note within renewed interest in standard NLP solvers for MPCCs, citing his own numbers and SQP theory (p. 2).
writing: Four-section note; claim in title and abstract; pre-empts the contrived-example objection; mechanism explained in plain words (pp. 1, 8).
limits_future: Remedy (4.13) proposed with typical constants but no proof or numerics; claim that any start admits failing parameters is unproved here (pp. 8-9).

title: The return of the active set method
contribution: Extended abstract proposing two active-set identification strategies (augmented-Lagrangian Cauchy step plus EQP with a filter for QP; a penalized l2 trust-region subproblem with bound-constrained dual for SLP-EQP), motivated by warm starts for integer optimization.
problem_entry: Active-set methods are more robust and warm-start better, which integer optimization needs; l-infinity trust-region bounds in SLP-EQP cause wasteful pivots (pp. 2-3).
key_idea: Cauchy point from a box-constrained augmented Lagrangian gives an active-set estimate, then EQP on inactive variables, with a filter replacing forcing sequences; for NLP an l2-penalized subproblem whose dual is a bound-constrained QP (pp. 2-3).
assumptions: QP with full-rank A and symmetric, possibly indefinite H; NLP with c(x) >= 0 (pp. 2-3).
proof_devices: Newton-step equivalence of the two steps for alpha = 1 (claimed), p. 2
filter convergence along the lines of Chin-Fletcher using a piecewise quadratic mu-radius relationship (claimed, no proof given), p. 3
experiments: n/a (only preliminary numerical experience called encouraging, p. 3)
positioning: Builds on LANCELOT, Dostal-Friedlander-Santos, Fletcher-Sainz de la Maza, Chin-Fletcher, Byrd-Gould-Nocedal-Waltz; cites Floudas and Grossmann for the integer motivation (pp. 2-4).
writing: Two method sketches and a three-sentence conclusion; hedged with We believe for the matrix-free claim (p. 4).
limits_future: Preliminary numerics only and no proofs in the note; both schemes implementable matrix-free (pp. 3-4).
